analysis:
Examined ci.yml metadata, the complete supplied patch and BASE source through line 1052. HEAD .github/workflows/ci.yml:53-64 adds conditional macOS routing lanes; :232-234, :477-479, :675-677, :878-880, :1010-1012, :1072-1074 and :1134-1136 make provider/SDK/cluster jobs depend on route and consume its runner selections. Lane counts match job conditions and shard inventories visible here. Test commands, timeouts, permissions, checkout credential persistence and push-only cache-save conditions are unchanged. No concrete authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or plaintext-exposure regression is established in this scope; T-041 cache controls are not modified.
The change expands the CI execution boundary from fixed Blacksmith macOS runners to potentially Sandbox-provided Macs. This matters to adversarial-provider assumptions (ADV-001, TB-003) and integrity of test evidence supporting A-017/T-054; it does not itself grant serving authorization or establish qualification. BASE :9-10 limits the workflow token to contents:read, and :19 restricts explicit cache saves to master/dev pushes, but these do not establish runner isolation or operator trust.
Integration should examine .github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml and its routing implementation for validated macOS destinations, fallback behavior, and lease duration across delayed summary jobs. Also reconcile the Sandbox runner contract for isolation from the Mac owner, cross-job cleanup, and protection of shared build caches/artifacts used by provider-ci-build (BASE :262-267, :505-522, :700-706). Those implementations/contracts are not supplied here; missing evidence is not proof of a vulnerability. Remaining material uncertainty is whether the newly eligible runner boundary preserves CI evidence and cache integrity.
